title: DO NOT BE AFRAID OF THEM

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them, because by this time tomorrow I will hand all of them, slain, over to Israel. You are to hamstring their horses and burn their chariots." - Josh 11:6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before Joshua sees a single enemy fall, God gives him the outcome. "By this time tomorrow." The victory is spoken as good as done while the enormous army is still camped and ready. God's word about the future is as certain as if it had already happened.

Then comes a strange command: hamstring the horses, burn the chariots. Israel is told to destroy the very weapons that made this army so fearsome. Why not keep them? Because God did not want Israel trusting in chariots for the next battle. The Lord was teaching them, and us, that their security would never rest in military hardware but in Him alone (Ps 20:7). The things that impress the world are often the very things God asks His people to let go of, so that our confidence stays fixed on Him.

We hear the tender heart of God in the first words: "Do not be afraid." This is the command He gives His people again and again across Scripture, and it is the same voice that stilled a storm and said to frightened disciples, "It is I; don't be afraid" (John 6:20). Fear shrinks when we hear who is speaking.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What "chariots" are you tempted to trust instead of God?
- How does hearing God say "do not be afraid" meet your fear today?
- Do you believe God's word about tomorrow as if it were already true?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, teach me to let go of the things I lean on instead of You. Quiet my fear with Your promise, and fix my trust on You alone. Amen.
